q: Write a SCIM filter that finds active users whose work email ends with @example.com.
must: uses a value filter: emails[type eq "work" and value ew "@example.com"] combined with active eq true
boolean true unquoted, strings in double quotes
explains that emails.type eq "work" and emails.value ew ... could match different emails
A: active eq true and emails[type eq "work" and value ew "@example.com"]  -- the [ ] value filter makes type and the domain test apply to the SAME email (emails.type eq "work" and emails.value ew "..." could match two different emails). Booleans are bare lowercase (true), strings in double quotes; emails.value is caseExact false so ew is case-insensitive. URL-encode it in GET (?filter=active%20eq%20true%20and%20emails%5Btype%20eq%20%22work%22...), or send it in POST /Users/.search. Filtering is optional (ServiceProviderConfig filter.supported). Checker: OK.
B: GET /Users?filter=active eq true and emails[type eq "work" and value ew "@example.com"]  -- uses a complex attribute filter (valuePath) so that type and value are matched on the SAME email entry; "ew" is the ends-with operator; string comparison on value is case-insensitive per the schema (caseExact=false for emails.value). Remember to URL-encode the filter in the query string. Writing emails.type eq "work" and emails.value ew "@example.com" would be weaker: the two conditions could match different email entries.

q: How do I remove a single member from a SCIM group with PATCH without touching the other members?
must: op remove with path members[value eq "<id>"]
schemas urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp and Operations array
warns that remove with path members alone removes all members (value on remove is not defined)
must_not: uses replace on members with the remaining list as the recommended way
uses an array index like members[0]
A: PATCH /Groups/{id} with a remove whose path selects the member by a value filter: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"remove","path":"members[value eq \"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646\"]"}]}. Do NOT send path "members" with a value array: RFC 7644 defines no value for remove, so a strict server removes ALL members; likewise replace on members replaces the whole membership. If the filter matches nothing the server returns 400 noTarget. Success is 200 with the group or 204 No Content. PATCH support is optional (ServiceProviderConfig patch.supported). Checker: OK.
B: Send PATCH /Groups/{id} with Content-Type application/scim+json and body {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"remove","path":"members[value eq \"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646\"]"}]}. The path uses a value filter on the multi-valued members attribute, so only the matching member is removed (RFC 7644 sec. 3.5.2.2). A remove with path "members" and no filter would remove ALL members. Do not use PUT, which replaces the whole members list. The server returns 200 with the resource or 204 No Content.

q: What paging parameters does SCIM use, is startIndex 0- or 1-based, and what do totalResults and itemsPerPage mean?
must: startIndex and count query parameters
startIndex is 1-based (values below 1 treated as 1)
totalResults = all matches, itemsPerPage = resources in this page; count 0 returns only totalResults
must_not: mentions cursor/nextLink as standard SCIM 2.0 RFC 7644 paging
A: SCIM uses startIndex and count as query parameters (RFC 7644 sec. 3.4.2.4). startIndex is 1-based (the first result is 1; values < 1 are treated as 1); count is the desired maximum number of results per page (a negative value is treated as 0; count=0 returns only totalResults, no Resources; the server may return fewer than requested). In the ListResponse (schema urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:ListResponse): totalResults = total number of results matching the query across all pages (REQUIRED); itemsPerPage = number of resources returned in this page; startIndex = 1-based index of the first result in this page; Resources = the array. itemsPerPage and startIndex are REQUIRED when paging is used.
B: Query parameters startIndex and count (RFC 7644 3.4.2.4); in POST /.search they are body fields. startIndex is 1-based (values < 1 are treated as 1); count is the requested page size (server may return fewer; count=0 returns only totalResults; negative treated as 0). In the ListResponse, totalResults is the total number of matches across all pages, itemsPerPage is the number of resources in this page, and startIndex echoes the 1-based index of the first returned result. Stop when startIndex + itemsPerPage > totalResults or a page is empty; index paging is not a snapshot, so results can shift if data changes.

q: My SCIM server returns errors as {"status": 400, "scimType": "invalidAttribute"}. Is that compliant?
must: status must be a JSON string ("400")
invalidAttribute is not a defined scimType; valid ones include invalidFilter, tooMany, uniqueness, mutability, invalidSyntax, invalidPath, noTarget, invalidValue, invalidVers, sensitive
schemas urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error required
A: No. Per RFC 7644 3.12 an error body must have "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"], "status" must be the HTTP status as a JSON string ("400", not the number 400), and "invalidAttribute" is not a defined scimType; valid ones are invalidFilter, tooMany, uniqueness, mutability, invalidSyntax, invalidPath, noTarget, invalidValue, invalidVers, sensitive (for a bad attribute value use invalidValue; for an unknown attribute in a filter, invalidFilter). Compliant: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"status":"400","scimType":"invalidValue","detail":"..."}. Clients should still tolerate numeric status and missing scimType. Checker: original FAIL (3 errors), corrected OK.
B: No. A SCIM error response must include "schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"] and status must be a JSON STRING containing the HTTP status code, e.g. {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"status":"400","scimType":"invalidValue","detail":"..."} (RFC 7644 sec. 3.12). Also "invalidAttribute" is not a defined scimType; the defined ones for 400 include invalidFilter, tooMany, uniqueness (409), mutability, invalidSyntax, invalidPath, noTarget, invalidValue, invalidVers, sensitive. Use invalidValue (or invalidSyntax/invalidPath as appropriate) and add a human-readable detail. The HTTP response status code must match.

q: Where does employeeNumber go in a SCIM User, and how do I filter on it?
must: Enterprise User extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User object, URN also listed in schemas
filter with the fully qualified path urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:employeeNumber eq "..."
must_not: puts employeeNumber at the top level of the User as correct
A: employeeNumber is not in the core User schema; it lives in the Enterprise User extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User (RFC 7643 sec. 4.3). Include the URN in "schemas" and put it under that key: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User","urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User"],"userName":"bjensen","urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User":{"employeeNumber":"701984"}}. Filter using the fully qualified attribute name: filter=urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:employeeNumber eq "701984" (URL-encoded). It is a string, so quote the value.
B: employeeNumber is in the Enterprise User extension (urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User), a single-valued readWrite string, not a core User attribute. Put it inside an object keyed by the URN and list the URN in schemas: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User","urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User"],"userName":"bjensen","urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User":{"employeeNumber":"701984"}}. Filter with the fully qualified path and a quoted string: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:employeeNumber eq "701984" (short "employeeNumber" works only if the server resolves it). Checker: OK.

q: What HTTP status should a SCIM server return when creating a user whose userName already exists?
must: 409 Conflict with scimType uniqueness (RFC 7644 3.3)
notes Table 9 lists scimType under 400, so clients should handle both
must_not: says 400 is the only correct answer without mentioning 3.3
A: 409 Conflict with scimType "uniqueness" (RFC 7644 3.3), since userName has uniqueness: server. Body: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"status":"409","scimType":"uniqueness","detail":"userName already exists"}. Note Table 9 lists scimType values under 400, so some servers return 400 uniqueness; servers should follow 3.3 (409) and clients should handle both.
B: 409 Conflict, with a SCIM Error body whose scimType is "uniqueness": {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"status":"409","scimType":"uniqueness","detail":"userName already exists"}. userName has uniqueness "server" in the core User schema (and is case-insensitive), so the server must reject a POST /Users that duplicates it (RFC 7644 sec. 3.3, 3.12).

q: Can a SCIM client set or change the id and meta attributes? What about password on read?
must: id and meta are readOnly, assigned by the server; use externalId for the client's identifier
password is writeOnly / returned never
must_not: says the client can choose id on POST
A: id is assigned by the service provider: it is readOnly (mutability) and the server ignores any id sent by the client on create; on PUT/PATCH it cannot be changed (attempting it can yield 400 mutability, or it is ignored). meta (resourceType, created, lastModified, location, version) is also readOnly and maintained by the server; client values are ignored. externalId, by contrast, is client-set. password has mutability writeOnly and returned "never": the client can set/replace it but the server must never return it in any response (GET, POST/PUT/PATCH responses, or list); it also cannot be used in filters meaningfully (returned never). Clients cannot read it.
B: No: id and meta are readOnly and assigned by the server; a client must not send them on create (POST) and cannot change them (PUT keeps readOnly values; a PATCH on them fails with 400 mutability). Use externalId (or userName) for the client-side key. password is writeOnly with returned: never, so it is never returned in any response (GET, create, PUT, PATCH, list), even if requested via attributes=. Clients may set it (if the server supports it; changePassword in ServiceProviderConfig).

q: Is filtering with gt/lt allowed on boolean attributes like active? And what about co on emails without a sub-attribute?
must: gt/ge/lt/le on boolean or binary must fail with 400 invalidFilter
complex attributes need a sub-attribute (emails.value) per 3.4.2.2, though the RFC's own examples use the short form
must_not: says gt on booleans is fine
A: No to gt/lt/ge/le on booleans: ordering operators are not allowed on boolean (and binary) attributes and the server must return 400 invalidFilter; use active eq true / active eq false. emails co "example.com" without a sub-attribute: RFC 7644 3.4.2.2 requires a sub-attribute for complex attributes (emails.value co "example.com"), although the RFC's own examples use the short form and many servers read it as emails.value; for portability write emails.value co "example.com" or emails[value co "example.com"]. Checker: active gt true -> ERROR; emails co ... -> WARNING.
B: No. Per RFC 7644 sec. 3.4.2.2, gt, ge, lt, le are not valid for boolean (and binary) attributes; the server should return 400 with scimType "invalidFilter". Booleans only support eq, ne and pr (e.g. active eq true). For emails co "x" with no sub-attribute: for a multi-valued complex attribute without a sub-attribute, the filter is applied to the "value" sub-attribute, i.e. emails co "example" behaves like emails.value co "example" and matches if any email value contains the string. Explicit emails.value or emails[value co "x"] is clearer.

q: How does a SCIM client find out whether a server supports PATCH, bulk, sorting and ETags?
must: GET /ServiceProviderConfig
patch, bulk (maxOperations, maxPayloadSize), filter (maxResults), changePassword, sort, etag supported flags
unsupported features may return 501
must_not: says there is no discovery mechanism
A: Query the discovery endpoint GET /ServiceProviderConfig (RFC 7644 sec. 4, schema RFC 7643 sec. 5). It returns complex attributes with a "supported" boolean: patch.supported, bulk.supported (plus bulk.maxOperations and bulk.maxPayloadSize), filter.supported (plus filter.maxResults), changePassword.supported, sort.supported, etag.supported, and authenticationSchemes. /ResourceTypes and /Schemas describe resource types and attributes. The endpoint does not need authentication normally (MAY be public).
B: GET /ServiceProviderConfig (RFC 7644 section 4, RFC 7643 5). It returns patch.supported, bulk.supported (+ bulk.maxOperations, bulk.maxPayloadSize), filter.supported (+ filter.maxResults), changePassword.supported, sort.supported, etag.supported and authenticationSchemes. Also read /ResourceTypes (endpoints, schema extensions) and /Schemas (attributes the server really implements). Do not send features advertised as false: the server may return 501 or ignore them.

q: Write a SCIM PATCH that changes only the user's work email address.
must: op replace with path emails[type eq "work"].value and the new value
PatchOp schemas and Operations
must_not: uses emails[0].value or a JSON Pointer path
A: PATCH /Users/{id} with {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"replace","path":"emails[type eq \"work\"].value","value":"b.jensen@example.com"}]}. The value filter selects only the work email and .value replaces just its address, leaving other emails and their type/primary untouched. No array indexes (emails[0] is invalid). If no work email exists, replace with a filter yields 400 noTarget; then use add on "emails" with [{"type":"work","value":"..."}]. Success: 200 with resource or 204. Checker: OK.
B: PATCH /Users/{id} with body {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"replace","path":"emails[type eq \"work\"].value","value":"bjensen@example.com"}]}. The value-path filter selects only the work email entry and replaces its value sub-attribute, leaving other emails untouched. If no work email exists, a replace with a filter that matches nothing returns 400 noTarget; in that case use op "add" with path "emails" and value [{"type":"work","value":"bjensen@example.com"}].

q: Is the Group displayName attribute required in SCIM?
must: yes: RFC 7643 section 4.2 says REQUIRED
the machine-readable schema in 8.7.1 says required false, a known inconsistency (erratum 5368)
must_not: says it is optional without noting the prose
A: Yes. RFC 7643 section 4.2 prose says Group displayName is REQUIRED, while the machine-readable schema in 8.7 says required: false (reported erratum 5368, not verified); the prose wins, so always send displayName when creating a Group. It is a readWrite string, caseExact false, uniqueness none. Servers that copied the 8.7 schema may accept groups without it, so check the provider's /Schemas.
B: The RFC is inconsistent. RFC 7643 sec. 4.2 (prose) says Group displayName is "A human-readable name for the Group. REQUIRED.", while the normative schema representation in sec. 8.7.1 lists displayName with "required": false (a known discrepancy). In practice treat it as required: always send displayName when creating a Group, since most service providers reject a Group without it. Its schema uniqueness is "none", though many providers enforce unique group names. members is optional.

q: In a SCIM bulk request, how can a later operation refer to a user created by an earlier operation in the same request?
must: POST operation with a bulkId (required for POST)
reference it as bulkId:<id> in later operations (e.g. in members value or path)
response carries status as a string per operation
must_not: says it is impossible within one request
A: Give each operation a bulkId and refer to it with "bulkId:<id>" in later operations (RFC 7644 sec. 3.7.2). Example: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:BulkRequest"],"Operations":[{"method":"POST","path":"/Users","bulkId":"qwerty","data":{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],"userName":"alice"}},{"method":"POST","path":"/Groups","bulkId":"ytrewq","data":{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"],"displayName":"Tour Guides","members":[{"type":"User","value":"bulkId:qwerty"}]}}]}. The server resolves bulkId:qwerty to the created id; bulkId is REQUIRED for POST operations. The response (BulkResponse) maps each bulkId to location/status. Servers must handle forward references and detect circular references; failOnErrors controls stopping after N errors.
B: Give the earlier POST a bulkId (required for POST operations), and reference it later as "bulkId:<id>" anywhere a resource id is expected, e.g. op1 {"method":"POST","path":"/Users","bulkId":"qwerty","data":{...User...}} then op2 {"method":"POST","path":"/Groups","bulkId":"ytrewq","data":{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"],"displayName":"Tour Guides","members":[{"type":"User","value":"bulkId:qwerty"}]}} (also usable in paths, e.g. /Users/bulkId:qwerty). The server substitutes the real id (RFC 7644 3.7.1/3.7.2) and must resolve or fail circular references. Bulk is optional (ServiceProviderConfig bulk.supported, maxOperations, maxPayloadSize; 413 if exceeded). Checker: OK.
